expectation: I expect oxygen to support further breakdown of the fuel in mitochondria, possibly preparing the way to remake ATP.

reaction: That distinction is useful, though the link between electron transfer and ATP production remains unclear.
reason: Adding ADP and phosphate is the only offered combination and addresses the goal of remaking ATP.

effect: The diagram connects electron transfer to ATP production through hydrogen-ion pumping and flow back through an ATP-making protein.
reaction: That fills in the previously unclear link between respiration and ATP production.
reason: The ion pump is the only offered combination and addresses the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect the pump to use ATP to move ions across the cell membrane, likely sodium and potassium.

effect: The pump completes the ATP cycle by using ATP to move sodium and potassium against their concentration differences; all chapter goals are complete.
reaction: The contrast with the earlier passive sodium channel makes the pump's purpose clear.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding ADP and phosphate was most worthwhile: the planned two-panel illustration connects electron transfer, hydrogen-ion flow and ATP production, filling an earlier explanatory gap.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding oxygen was less satisfying on its own because the initial result did not explain how electron transfer drives ATP production; the next result supplied that connection.

surprise.text: The glucose breakdown illustration showed ATP production in the cytosol, outside mitochondria, alongside pyruvate formation.

arbitrary.text: No action lacked a clear purpose, although every decision had only one offered combination, leaving little meaningful choice.

continue.text: I would continue to see how later constructions connect cellular processes to tissues and organs, though I would hope for more choices.
